description.value: The study evaluates voxel-based partial least squares classification of FDG PET images for differentiating normal controls, Alzheimer's disease, and frontotemporal dementia across scanners, including inter-scanner ratio-image normalization.
Retrospective and prospective clinical databases from two sites and three scanners were evaluated using supervised classification with training and test data.

value: The baseline “in-scanner” setup yielded classification accuracies between 89% and 98% for the three scanners, with an overall accuracy of 94%.
Training the classifier on a different scanner (“x-scanner”) severely degraded accuracy to 70 to 84% for the various scanner combinations, with average accuracy of 79%.
Increasing the amount of training data from a second mismatched scanner (“train-other”) did not have a notable impact on classification accuracy (80%).
Finally, adding training data from the correct scanner as well (“train-all”), i.e. training on all three scanners, improved accuracy to 91%.
